items.title: `uv add --index <name>=...` in a workspace member can change existing dependencies' index
items.reason: Closest existing bug for the workspace mutation: adding through a member copies an index into that member and can shadow the root definition. It does not cover credential-variant equality or the lock conflict, so the new report should remain separate.

items.title: Support referencing indexes by name via `--index` and `--default-index`
items.reason: This merged change supports resolving a named index from workspace configuration and copying it into a child package. Its review explicitly discusses whether the copy is necessary and whether indexes should be deduplicated by URL.

items.title: `uv add --index ...` adds implicit indexes to files which are not consulted for them
items.reason: Same command and workspace-member persistence path, but this issue tracks persisted member indexes being ignored during candidate search rather than root/member credential variants being treated as conflicting.

items.title: Search a workspace member's own indexes during resolution
items.reason: Open proposed fix for astral-sh/uv#20678. It makes member indexes participate in resolution but does not change credential-sensitive index equality, so it does not subsume this report.

related.search_scope: Repository-wide open and closed issue searches and open, closed, and merged pull-request searches covered the exact `Requirements contain conflicting indexes` error, `uv add --index` workspace persistence, root/member index copying and shadowing, duplicate and same-endpoint terminology, username and credential variants, CodeArtifact, URL canonicalization, lockfile validation, and historical fixes. Candidate threads and their cross-references were inspected. astral-sh/uv#18250 confirms separately supplied indexes are not matched by URL but has a different environment-configuration trigger. astral-sh/uv#20635 and astral-sh/uv#20753 concern trailing-slash lock validation; astral-sh/uv#14511 explains why slash normalization can be semantically unsafe. astral-sh/uv#9942 shares the conflict error but involves genuinely different package indexes under extras, and astral-sh/uv#8565 concerns credential-cache reuse, so those were ruled out.

type_reason: Repository source confirms a correctness gap rather than a support question or new capability request. The add path compares an incoming index only with indexes in the target member document, then removes URL credentials when persisting it; it does not reuse an equivalent root entry. Separately, the resolver's per-package conflict check compares index metadata directly, so credential-bearing and credential-free forms can be treated as different even though canonical URL comparison elsewhere strips credentials. Existing issues cover adjacent workspace-copy behavior, but none tracks this credential-variant conflict closely enough to make astral-sh/uv#21281 a duplicate.
summary: The closest history is the known workspace-member index copying and persistence behavior in astral-sh/uv#17610, astral-sh/uv#17455, and astral-sh/uv#20678. astral-sh/uv#20922 addresses whether copied member indexes are searched, not whether credential variants are equivalent. No existing issue or pull request covers both the unwanted duplicate entry and the resulting credential-variant conflict.
draft_response:
Thanks for the report. This is a bug. The current add path can copy a workspace index into the member configuration, and index URLs are persisted without embedded credentials. The resolver can then treat that member entry and the credential-bearing root entry as conflicting indexes for the same package.

This overlaps with the workspace index-copying behavior in astral-sh/uv#17610 and astral-sh/uv#20678, but neither tracks the credential-variant conflict, so this should remain separate. Could you provide a minimal root/member pair of `pyproject.toml` files and clarify whether the `--index` argument is an index name or a URL? Please use only a dummy endpoint and placeholder username, with no real credentials. That will let us cover both the unwanted member entry and the subsequent `uv lock` failure in a regression test.
